Register the property with customized getter and setter.
In the custom setter, update the property and call `signal_property()` to avoid the infinite loop: `set_property -> setter -> set_property -> ...`

Done. Registered both PowerCap and PowerCapEnable with a custom
setter and a custom getter (direct member assignment + signal_property())
Done

Drop this as no re-broadcast here is needed if followed the approach mentioned above.
Done

Consider dropping this. 
I think registering the property with a custom getter that returns live members,
and update the property with a custom setter that assigns value + call `signal_property()` from the internal paths.

In this way, the setter callback then only ever runs on a D-Bus client write, and the flag is unnecessary.
Done

An alternatives: Register these properties inside `Inventory` itself using `register_property_r` with a getter lambda that returns the `Inventory`-owned member. The optional then becomes the single source of truth, and `getMinPowerCap()` / `getMaxPowerCap()` keep returning it for the setter's range check.

*PS: It should be `register_property()` instead of `register_property_r`.
Apologize for typo.

Kept register_property_r since it is the canonical read-only overload and 
the 4-arg register_property would require providing a no-op/reject setter just to make them read-only, which is more boilerplate.
Thanks.
LGTM
Is it possible to do register_property in GPU Device class? can we use plain set_property method to update the value once it is available and also populate the member data at the same time?
Done — reverted to the patchset 1 approach: Min/Max/Default are registered in the GPU device class and published via set_property (updating the value and member together).
Please add unit test cases for these functions.
Done
Using reference to const and than copying it would be preferred pattern here in my opinion to avoid constructing the object twice.

Taking the shared_ptr by value + std::move is the recommended sink idiom: an rvalue moves in with no refcount bump, an lvalue copies once (same as const-ref + copy). Happy to switch if you'd still prefer it.

Please correct me if I am wrong, but with by value and move, we are doing 2 shared_ptr constructor calls and 1 ref count update, with reference to const and copy, we will do 1 shared_ptr constructor call and 1 ref count update. So reference to const is preferred in my opinion and if we always expect caller to pass an rvalue we should make the constructor parameter an rvalue reference.
You're right. Our caller always passes an lvalue (NvidiaGpuDevice's inventory member). Switched to const reference + copy. Thanks.

This would also update the value on dbus right? That would be incorrect if Set operation using MCTP VDM command fails. Calling update after the Set operation would anyway update the value on dbus.

Done — the setter no longer writes the exposed value. PowerCap/PowerCapEnable are written only in the GetPowerLimits response handler; a SetPowerLimits success triggers an immediate GetPowerLimits, so the value reflects the device (and a failed write leaves no stale value). The requested cap is kept in a member so a combined PATCH isn't lost.
Do we need this since we have custom getter for property?
Done
remove else block and return from if block to align with pattern in this daemon.

Call update function after the set is completed to update the latest value on dbus.

If there are simultaneous set-property calls on both PowerCap and PowerCapEnable, the call that's processed later might hit this error. It's better to setup a timer to collect both set-property call, maybe with something like this - https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/87107/3/src/nvidia-gpu/NvidiaMetricReport.cpp#73?

Done — applyPendingPowerLimit now clears both requestedPowerCapWatts and pendingEnable once the coalesced burst is dispatched (snapshotting the cap first so a combined PATCH still applies it). 
A cap set while disabled is no longer silently re-applied on a later unrelated enable.
